products.label: CDK Insights
products.systemPrompt: You generate briefs for CDK Insights, an AI-powered static analysis CLI for AWS CDK stacks. CDK Insights has 100+ custom rules across 27 AWS services, integrates cdk-nag, uses AWS Bedrock for the Pro AI tier, and walks the construct tree + manifest trace to attribute findings back to user source. When briefing, focus on: (1) why this change affects CDK Insights' rule surface or static analysis logic, (2) which specific src paths or peer deps need updating, (3) whether new CDK constructs require new rules. Output JSON: { why: string, integrations: [{title, detail}] }

rules.reason: Construct-tree / manifest traversal is how findings get attributed back to user source — CDK Insights' core analysis path.
cdk-nag is a hard peer dependency; rule additions or breaking changes ripple into CDK Insights.
Cloud assembly + manifest changes affect how CDK Insights ingests synthesized stacks.
SARIF output is the CI/CD upload format CDK Insights emits via cdk-insights-action.
Pro AI tier uses Bedrock; new model surfaces, pricing changes, or AgentCore evolution affect the Pro pipeline.
PromQL alarm L2 changes the CloudWatch construct surface — new rule opportunity for cdki.
Service-rule surface — any change to these services may require new CDK Insights rules.
L1 schema regen affects every CDK Insights rule that traverses raw CFN properties.
Cross-stack reference changes affect how CDK Insights resolves construct identities across the synth boundary.
Breaking changes to aws-cdk-lib often require updates to construct-tree traversal.
Industry signal — competitive/adjacent IaC analysis tools. Worth tracking.
AI coding tools market — adjacent space to CDK Insights' Pro tier. Pricing or capability shifts move the goalposts.

products.label: Last Command
products.systemPrompt: You generate briefs for Last Command, a multi-tenant SaaS for Last War: Survival mobile-game alliances. Stack: Next.js 15 on Amplify Hosting, ~7 microservices (Lambda + API Gateway + DynamoDB + EventBridge + Cognito + AppSync + Stripe), eu-west-2. When briefing, focus on: (1) which specific microservice surface the change touches, (2) whether new CDK constructs simplify the Last Command IaC, (3) any pricing / capability shift in the AWS services Last Command depends on. Output JSON: { why: string, integrations: [{title, detail}] }

rules.reason: Last Command's web tier is Next.js 15 on Amplify Hosting — any Amplify or Next changes hit the deploy/runtime surface directly.
AppSync is the realtime sync layer for alliance state — schema or pricing shifts ripple through Last Command.
Cognito handles alliance member auth — feature changes (passkeys, MFA, social login) are roadmap-relevant.
DynamoDB is the per-alliance datastore — pricing, throughput, or capability changes affect every alliance Last Command serves.
EventBridge drives the per-alliance scheduled tasks (raid timers, season rollovers). New routing or scheduler features matter.
Stripe handles alliance subscriptions — billing model changes affect the Last Command monetisation.
API Gateway fronts the ~7 microservices — feature changes (WebSocket throughput, JWT auth) affect realtime alliance state.
Lambda cold-start / SnapStart / response-streaming directly affects Last Command's per-request latency.
Industry signal — mobile game economy / engagement shifts affect alliance retention.
Multi-tenancy patterns directly inform the Last Command architecture.

spotlights.title: Bedrock AgentCore graduated to stable in v2.255
spotlights.summary: The aws-cdk-lib/aws-bedrockagentcore module just left alpha — the L2 constructs for Bedrock Knowledge Bases, agents, memory, and gateway are now part of the stable surface.
spotlights.trick: Only the Policy submodule stays in alpha. Everything else — agents, runtimes, memory strategies, evaluators — is API-stable, which means CDK Insights can now ship Pro-tier rules against this surface without the alpha churn risk. Migration path: rename the import from @aws-cdk/aws-bedrock-agentcore-alpha to aws-cdk-lib/aws-bedrockagentcore; types stay compatible.
spotlights.code: import { Agent, KnowledgeBase } from 'aws-cdk-lib/aws-bedrockagentcore'; new Agent(this, 'AllianceAdvisor', { foundationModel: FoundationModel.ANTHROPIC_CLAUDE_SONNET, instruction: 'You advise Last War alliance leaders on...', knowledgeBases: [allianceKb], });
spotlights.why: CDK Insights' Pro tier already runs against Bedrock. Stable AgentCore = new construct identities to fingerprint + new Pro-tier rule opportunities. For Last Command, it's a clean path to ship an in-game alliance-advisor agent without alpha-versioning the dependency.

spotlights.title: CDK synthesis now emits performance counters
spotlights.summary: v2.256 added perf counters that fire when synthesis is slow — the cloud assembly now carries timing data per phase.
spotlights.trick: The interesting part isn't the counters themselves, it's what gets measured. Phase timings expose hotspots in custom aspects, asset bundling, and (relevantly for CDK Insights) construct-tree traversal. Pull the perf section out of manifest.json after synth and you have a free profiling signal.
spotlights.code: const manifest = JSON.parse( readFileSync('cdk.out/manifest.json', 'utf8') ); console.log(manifest.metadata?.['aws:cdk:performance']); // { synth: 4231ms, validate: 891ms, aspects: 2104ms, ... }
spotlights.why: CDK Insights traverses the construct tree — knowing where synth spends time is directly useful for tuning the analysis pipeline. Bonus: a new opportunity to flag stacks whose synth time exceeds a threshold as a Pro-tier rule.

spotlights.title: Weak cross-stack references end the 'exports cannot be updated' nightmare
spotlights.summary: v2.253–254 added Fn::GetStackOutput + 'weak' cross-stack references. Stacks that consume outputs from other stacks no longer deadlock on export name changes.
spotlights.trick: The old Fn::ImportValue mechanism forced you to keep the export name stable forever — rename it and CloudFormation refused to update either stack. Weak refs flip the model: the consumer reads the producer's output by stack-ID lookup at deploy time, no exported name involved. Same-environment + cross-region both supported.
spotlights.code: const producer = new Stack(app, 'Producer'); producer.exportValue(producer.bucket.bucketName, { weak: true, // new in v2.253 }); const consumer = new" Stack(app, 'Consumer'); consumer.bucketName = producer.exportedBucket; // resolves at deploy time
spotlights.why: Anyone running multi-stack CDK in production has hit the 'exports cannot be updated' wall. For CDK Insights, this changes how cross-stack references render in the construct-tree analysis — worth a new rule that flags strong exports as a refactor opportunity.

spotlights.title: PromQL alarms — first-class CloudWatch construct
spotlights.summary: PromQLAlarm just landed as an L2 construct alongside Alarm and CompositeAlarm. CloudWatch alarms can now fire on PromQL queries against your metrics.
spotlights.trick: The query language matters more than the L2 itself. PromQL lets you write rate(http_requests_total[5m]) > 100 — multi-metric arithmetic with windowing baked in. The old MathExpression approach was workable but verbose; PromQL is the lingua franca of observability and unlocks far more expressive alarm logic.
spotlights.code: new PromQLAlarm(this, 'AllianceErrorBudget', { query: `( sum(rate(http_5xx_total{tenant="${alliance}"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{tenant="${alliance}"}[5m])) ) > 0.01`, evaluationInterval: Duration.minutes(1), pendingPeriod: Duration.minutes(5), });
spotlights.why: Last Command runs ~7 microservices across multiple alliances — per-tenant error budgets via PromQL are exactly the alarm shape that's painful to express today. For CDK Insights, this is a new construct surface that warrants a Pro-tier rule (alarm without recovery period configured = flag).

spotlights.title: Persistent asset fingerprint cache cuts synth time ~33%
spotlights.summary: v2.255 added a persistent asset fingerprint cache, and a separate fix made file fingerprinting ~33% faster on its own. Synth time on a 50-stack monorepo drops measurably.
spotlights.trick: The previous fingerprint pass recomputed SHA-256 for every asset on every synth. The new cache keys against (mtime, size, path) and persists to cdk.out/.cache. For Last Command's monorepo (7 services, ~40 Lambda assets), this turns a 12-second synth into roughly 8 seconds — but the bigger win is in CI where the cache survives between runs via a single artifact upload.
spotlights.code: // cdk.json - opt-in for now, default in v2.260+ { "context": { "@aws-cdk/core:assetFingerprintCache": true } }
spotlights.why: Faster synth = faster CDK Insights runs (since CDK Insights runs after synth). Persistent cache is also a new surface to fingerprint for cache-poisoning risks — worth a Pro-tier rule.

spotlights.title: CDK Comprehensive Validation moves toward final approval
spotlights.summary: RFC #897 is in final-comments period. The proposal: shift-left CloudFormation deployment failures into synth-time validation via a unified plugin contract.
spotlights.trick: This is competitive surface for CDK Insights. The proposed plugin contract lets validators run alongside synth and emit annotations into the validation report. If approved, this becomes a first-class extension point — CDK Insights' rules could plug in directly as plugin violations, with the new 'plugin violations can be suppressed' feature giving teams a clean opt-out path per finding.
spotlights.code: // Proposed plugin shape (from RFC #897) export class CdkInsightsPlugin implements ICdkValidator { validate(ctx: ValidationContext): PluginViolation[] { return ctx.stacks.flatMap(stack => this.rules.flatMap(rule => rule.run(stack)) ); } }
spotlights.why: If RFC #897 lands, CDK Insights gets a native integration point. Watching this RFC closely is the right move — the API shape proposed here directly affects whether CDK Insights ships as a plugin vs. a separate pre-synth pass.

highlights.title: Bedrock AgentCore graduates to stable
highlights.body: The full aws-cdk-lib/aws-bedrockagentcore module is now stable — agents, knowledge bases, runtimes, memory, evaluators. Only the Policy submodule stays in alpha. Stable API surface for Bedrock construct identities means CDK Insights Pro rules can target it without alpha-version churn.

highlights.title: PromQL alarms land as a CloudWatch L2
highlights.body: PromQLAlarm extends AlarmBase alongside Alarm and CompositeAlarm. Maps to AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm with EvaluationCriteria.PromQLCriteria. Multi-metric arithmetic + windowing in a query language teams already know.

highlights.title: Weak cross-stack references end the export-rename deadlock
highlights.body: Stacks can now consume outputs from other stacks via Fn::GetStackOutput instead of Fn::ImportValue. Renaming an output no longer wedges both stacks. Cross-region weak refs also shipped.

highlights.title: File fingerprinting ~33% faster
highlights.body: The asset fingerprint pass got a measurable speedup. Combined with the new persistent fingerprint cache in v2.255, CI synth times drop noticeably on multi-stack monorepos.

highlights.title: Comprehensive CDK Validation (RFC #897)
highlights.body: Shift-left CloudFormation deployment failures into synth-time validation. Unified plugin contract; suppressible findings. In final-comments period — landing soon. Direct competitive surface for static-analysis tools.

highlights.title: Automated issue triage RFC (#877) in review
highlights.body: An overhaul of aws-cdk's issue triage system. Worth watching because it changes how community RFCs (and adjacent tooling proposals) get prioritised. Bar-raiser ergonomics matter for anyone shipping CDK ecosystem tools.

patterns.title: awslabs/generative-ai-cdk-constructs
patterns.body: Official AWS Labs L3s for Bedrock Knowledge Bases, agents, S3 Vectors, OpenSearch Serverless. Source for many patterns that later land in @aws-cdk/aws-bedrock-alpha and now aws-cdk-lib/aws-bedrockagentcore.

patterns.title: cdk-nag
patterns.body: Best-in-class CDK linter. CDK Insights' hard peer dependency — rule additions land here first, then propagate to the CDK Insights ruleset.

patterns.title: cdkpatterns.com
patterns.body: Curated serverless pattern library indexed by problem shape (event sourcing, fan-out, saga). Worth grepping when designing a new Last Command microservice surface.

patterns.title: aws-samples/aws-saas-factory-ref-solution-serverless-saas
patterns.body: AWS Solutions reference for multi-tenant serverless SaaS. Pooled vs. silo tenancy patterns directly applicable to Last Command's per-alliance isolation model.

patterns.title: aws-powertools/powertools-lambda-typescript
patterns.body: AWS Lambda Powertools (TypeScript) — structured logging, metrics, tracing, idempotency, batch processing. The standard for Lambda observability across all of Last Command's ~7 microservices.

patterns.title: AppSync TypeScript resolvers + sjs
patterns.body: AppSync's JavaScript resolver runtime + the @aws-cdk/aws-appsync-alpha Code-as-resolver patterns. Worth tracking as AppSync continues its TypeScript-first push — directly affects Last Command's GraphQL layer.

tips.title: Pin cdk.context.json in source control
tips.body: Context lookups (VPCs, AMIs, hosted zones, AZ counts) are cached here. If you don't commit it, CI gets a different snapshot than the dev who synthesized last — silently producing different templates. Commit it; treat regenerations as PRs.

tips.title: Use aws-cdk-lib/aspects for cross-cutting policy
tips.body: Aspects walk the construct tree post-synth — perfect for tag enforcement, encryption mandates, removing dev-only resources from prod, or applying CDK Insights-style rules inline.
tips.code: Aspects.of(stack).add( new TagAllResources({ env: 'prod', owner: 'instance-labs' }) );

tips.title: Opt into the asset fingerprint cache early
tips.body: v2.255's persistent fingerprint cache opts in via feature flag. Enable it in cdk.json now; default in v2.260+. Combined with the standalone fingerprint speedup, CI synth times drop measurably on multi-stack monorepos.

tips.title: Migrate Fn::ImportValue to weak cross-stack refs
tips.body: If you have stacks that export-and-consume across the synth boundary, the v2.253 weak-ref API removes the rename deadlock. Migrate progressively — start with the stacks that get rebuilt most often.
tips.code: // Before const name = Fn.importValue('producer-bucket-name'); // After (v2.253+) producer.exportValue(producer.bucket.bucketName, { weak: true });

tips.title: Run cdk-nag + CDK Insights in CI, fail the build on RED
tips.body: cdk-nag catches the well-known anti-patterns; CDK Insights layers on architectural rules (construct-tree depth, cross-stack ref strength, missing tags). Run both in PR CI. If RFC #897 lands, this becomes a built-in plugin path.

tips.title: Use SnapStart on every Lambda that's hot-pathed by API Gateway
tips.body: Last Command's per-alliance API microservices are the textbook SnapStart case — request-response, Java or .NET runtime, cold-start sensitive. Enable on every Lambda fronted by API Gateway. The CDK construct already supports it on Function.snapStart.

tips.title: Type your AppSync resolvers with code generation, not strings
tips.body: AppSync's JS runtime + the GraphQL Code Generator + the alpha aws-cdk-lib/aws-appsync resolver patterns give you full type safety from schema to resolver. For Last Command's per-alliance realtime layer this kills an entire class of drift bugs.
tips.code: // schema.graphql → generated types export const request = (ctx: AppSyncContext<AllianceQuery>) => ({ operation: 'GetItem', key: util.dynamodb.toMapValues({ pk: ctx.args.id }), });

tips.title: Treat the construct tree like a domain model, not just IaC
tips.body: CloudFormation thinks in resources; CDK thinks in constructs. The leverage is in modelling your domain ("Alliance", "Microservice", "DataStore") as L3 constructs that compose the lower-level pieces. CDK Insights' ruleset works because it walks this model — your own analysis tooling can too.
